newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Fletcher completes 2nd U.S. bond issue.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Fletcher completes 2nd U.S. bond issue.

text.p: Fletcher Challenge Ltd said on Thursday it had completed its second issue, of US$350 million, to the U.S. public bond markets.
Due to good investor demand, the group elected to accept US$50 million above the original target for the issue.
A 100 percent-owned finance subsidiary, Fletcher Challenge Capital Canada, will issue US$200 million of 7.5 percent notes due 2007, and US$150 million of 7.875 percent notes due 2017.
These notes are unconditionally guaranteed by Fletcher Challenge and Fletcher Challenge Industries.
The first issue of these debt instruments, known in the market parlance as Yankee Bonds, was made in June 1996.
At that time, Fletcher Challenge issued US$250 million of 7.75 percent notes due in 2006 and US$150 million of 8.25 percent notes due in 2016.
Fletcher Challenge chief executive officer Hugh Fletcher said he was delighted with the continued support of US investors of issues by Fletcher Challenge.
He said the latest issue would further reduce average borrowing costs and lengthen the group's maturity profile. The proceeds of the issue would be used to pay down existing debt.
The Yankee Bond offering was led by Merrill Lynch and co-managed by CS First Boston, Morgan Stanley and UBS Securities.
